chunk_findings.detail: The helper is called for every explicit selector (`chunks`, `commit`, `base`, `delta`, `full`, `force`) but only checks whether the gate's latest run has `terminated_by`; it never compares the new request's scope with that terminated run. After a SIGTERMed full review, a run such as `ddflow review --gate critic --chunks src/new.py --reason ...` will log `asked for explicitly (repeats the review terminated by SIGTERM)` even though the specified chunks were not part of the terminated run, so the log falsely states the review is a repeat.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/scope.py:_repeat_of_terminated

chunk_findings.detail: The new filter only drops a stale edge when the holder is present and still has a lease (`it is not None and it.lease is not None`). If the named holder has released its lease (`it.lease is None`) or is no longer in `st.items`, the edge falls through to `out.setdefault(item_id, []).append(waiter)`. That keeps the exact false `YIELD REQUESTED` this change says it removes, now for a released/absent holder instead of a disjoint one. Repro: after T1 releases its lease, `WG.wait_for_graph(st, cfg, now)` still returns `{"T2": ["T1"]}`; `contended` then returns `{"T1": ["T2"]}` even though T1 has no live lease, contrary to the new contract (“limited to … the item's LIVE lease”).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leasebreak.py:contended

chunk_findings.detail: This regression never establishes that a stale wait edge exists before it asserts the edge is gone. It goes straight from the refused widening to `run_cli(repo, "update", "T2", "--globs", "", agent=B)` and then checks `LB.contended(...).get("T1")` is empty, but it does not first assert that T2 is in `WG.standing` after the refused widening (or after the empty narrow). If the empty-glob update clears T2's pending wait along with its globs, or if the refused widening records no wait in this path, `LB.contended` would already be empty without any filter and the test would pass even against the unfixed short-circuit the test is meant to catch. Add the same standing assertion as the first test to pin the stale edge before asserting it is removed.
